newsitem.title: USA: S&P says California note season on track.
newsitem.headline: S&P says California note season on track.

text.p: California's 1997 tax and revenue anticipation note (TRAN) season should run smoothly, as concerns raised by the Orange County bankruptcy continue to die down, Standard & Poor's Corp said Monday.
The rating agency said 1997 TRAN volume should mirror last year's season with one major exception -- the state of California is expected to issue less short-term debt.
"The after-effects of Orange County are diminishing for local short-term debt issuers," S&P added in its CreditWeek Municipal newsletter.
In 1995, the California TRAN market was hurt by Orange County's bankruptcy. Debt issues were unexpectedly delayed because investors demanded heightened protection against investment risk, S&P said.
The bankruptcy's fallout extended into 1996, when issuers turned to third party paying agents, fiscal agents, trustees and guaranteed investment contracts to allay investor concerns.
S&P said it expected fewer issuers in 1997 to use paying agents and investment contracts for 12 month notes because Orange County concerns are diminishing.

California's TRAN season runs from mid-May to the end of June. During the state's 1996 TRAN season, S&P said it rated 94 issues and nearly all of the par amount of $11.5 billion of the TRANs sold by counties, cities and school districts.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments.
The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
